topic: how an IKEA employee taking the legs off a table helped make flat-pack furniture normal
storyAngle: A table that would not fit in a car turned into a business model where the customer does the assembly.
doNotClaim: Do NOT say IKEA invented flat-pack furniture; IKEA itself says Lundgren helped popularize it.
Do not say the motive was shipping cost or damage; the sources say only that the table would not fit in the car.
Do not say whether the legs were sawed or unscrewed; accounts differ. The date is IKEA's account; some sources date the Lovet table to 1959.

facts.claim: According to IKEA's own story, in 1956 IKEA employee Gillis Lundgren could not fit a table into his car, so he took the legs off.
facts.note: IKEA page plus Wallpaper; date varies by source

facts.claim: IKEA says Lundgren helped popularize flat-pack furniture; it does not claim he invented the idea.
IKEA customers assemble flat-pack furniture themselves after buying it.
